posts.author: MushroomCake28
posts.body:
It needs to be on a character sheet. If you start the character sheet's filename with $, the engine will split it into 12 areas (3x4) and the dimension of a single character will be the image's width / 3 by the image's height / 4.
If by default the car is 3 tiles width by 2 tiles height, then your char file needs to be 432x384 (3 tiles width x 48 pixels per tile x 3 = 432, and 2 tiles height x 48 pixels x 4 = 384). Just use photoshop or GIMP to format it correctly.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
@RenGames
in your example, you used two different example pictures.
the first example (the one you placed as a tileset) clearly shows something formatted as a sprite (each car has 3x4 individual pictures in the four directions), and sprites are needed for events and should be placed in characters.
in your second example, that looks like something that is formatted as tiles (only single version of cars) and those would have to be placed in tiles instead of events.
That is why you were referred to the asset standards - it doesn't matter what the pictures show, it's the structure of the picture that determies whether it needs to be used as a sprite or as a tile.
